CHANGES (list ALL modifications, one or multiple):

Change #1: [Category: Model Architecture]
- What: In model_design, add a jointly trained, bias-free linear projection of the last valid contextualized history vector to the existing graph-user attention query, before tanh attention scoring. Use a zero contribution for empty histories and update architecture metadata and the predictor writer to restore this same attention module.
- Why: The current query depends only on the graph-user embedding; conditioning attention explicitly on the latest event should help distinguish a user's current purchase intent from their broader interests.

---

WHY current solution limited:
- Root cause: Relative positions and causal convolutions contextualize attention keys and values, but the query does not explicitly adapt to the latest observed item.
- Evidence: This limitation follows directly from history_query(u) in encode_history; the measured Electronics HR@10 of 0.465, versus 0.650–0.700 in the other categories, motivates testing better intent conditioning but does not establish the cause of that gap.

HOW these changes address it:
- Mechanism: The latest contextualized event will condition which earlier purchases receive attention, allowing the existing history summary and gate to adapt to recent intent within one jointly trained network.
- Expected improvement: Test the hypothesis of a 0.005–0.015 absolute macro HR@10 gain over the current 0.6213; accept improvement only if independently measured by the pinned host evaluator.
- Synergy (if multiple changes): No separate experimental change; serialization and predictor updates only preserve the modified architecture at inference.

KEEP UNCHANGED (must explicitly list):
- Random seed: preprocessing seed=0 and training seed=42.
- Data split: identical supplied training and validation splits; no hidden test access or additional data.
- Model: one independently trained GraphRecommender and one selected checkpoint per category, retaining all four categories and dataset routing; no ensembles or checkpoint averaging.
- Architecture otherwise: graph propagation, supervised-edge masking, residual causal convolution, relative positions, fusion gate, tied item vectors, and jointly learned item bias.
- Training: current prefix sampling, negative sampling, loss, regularization, optimizer, batch size, steps, epoch limit, patience, and category time limits.
- Evaluation: macro-average validation HR@10, 200 users per category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed=42, and the unchanged host evaluator.
- Execution: single GPU, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, and identical model inference logic in local validation and working/predict.py.
